final_candidates.decision_summary: AlphaMissense pathogenicity 0.998 and very rare MSA frequency support a strongly damaging substitution likely to abolish CBS activity.
AlphaMissense pathogenicity 0.996 and rare MSA frequency indicate a highly disruptive substitution at a conserved glycine.
K119 is the PLP-binding lysine; mutating it removes the cofactor anchor, and AlphaMissense 0.987 plus low MSA tolerance support clean loss of enzyme activity.

stop_reason.detail: Additional evidence is unlikely to change the Top-3 because the leading candidates already have strong phenotype and evolutionary intolerance signals.

history.rationale: K119 is the PLP-anchoring lysine; alanine cannot form the covalent internal aldimine with PLP, abolishing catalysis.
AlphaMissense 0.987 strongly supports pathogenic/LOF effect; K119 is the PLP-binding active-site lysine, making this mechanistically compelling.
K119 is the PLP-binding lysine; mutating it should abolish activity, and AlphaMissense 0.987 plus low MSA tolerance support this.
Same PLP-binding lysine; methionine lacks the nucleophilic amine required for PLP Schiff-base formation.
AlphaMissense 0.976 strongly supports LOF; same active-site position as K119A.
Same PLP-site lysine as K119A; M is entirely absent from homologs (0.0), strongly supporting damage, though AlphaMissense is slightly lower and bulkier side chain may affect folding.
Active-site cysteine likely involved in PLP/homocysteine reaction chemistry; alanine removes the reactive thiol.
AlphaMissense 0.732 is pathogenic but lower than top candidates; retained but ranked lower.
AlphaMissense 0.732 is only moderate, and MSA frequency 0.0471 is rare but not decisive; retained as low-priority backup.
Active-site arginine likely coordinates the PLP phosphate or substrate carboxylate; alanine disrupts charge and hydrogen bonding.
AlphaMissense 0.740 is pathogenic but weaker than top candidates.
AlphaMissense 0.740 and moderately rare MSA frequency (0.0845) keep it as a lower-confidence backup.
Conserved glycine in the PLP-binding loop; glutamate introduces steric bulk and negative charge incompatible with cofactor pocket geometry.
AlphaMissense 0.982 strongly supports LOF; high-confidence candidate.
AlphaMissense is high (0.982), but MSA mutant frequency 0.214 among homologs indicates unexpected evolutionary tolerance, slightly reducing confidence relative to K119A.
Threonine in the conserved PLP-binding motif; replacement by large hydrophobic methionine likely disrupts cofactor interactions.
AlphaMissense 0.863 supports damaging effect but lower than top candidates.
AlphaMissense 0.863 and rare MSA frequency (0.0119) support a damaging substitution, though not as strongly as the top candidates.
Glycine in the PLP-binding loop; introduction of a charged bulky side chain likely destabilizes the active-site conformation.
AlphaMissense 0.996 is nearly maximal pathogenicity; strong LOF candidate.
AlphaMissense 0.996 and rare MSA frequency (0.0233) both strongly support LOF.
Glycine in the PLP-binding loop; glutamate substitution likely disrupts the tight loop required for PLP binding.
AlphaMissense 0.998 is the highest pathogenicity score in the pool; top LOF candidate.
AlphaMissense 0.998 and very rare MSA frequency (0.0118) both support a damaging loss-of-function substitution.
Conserved aspartate likely hydrogen-bonds the PLP pyridine nitrogen; alanine removes this essential contact.
AlphaMissense 0.526 is ambiguous and below a clear pathogenic threshold; weak LOF signal not worth retaining.
